meta.description: Fires when triage marks an existing-client message high priority. Posts to the client-service Slack channel and opens a task for the owning advisor with a 4-hour due date. Deliberately narrow: this is the one intersection where a false positive costs an extra Slack message and a false negative costs a client.

nodes.name: New triage result
nodes.notes: Polling rather than a webhook so a missed minute self-heals on the next tick instead of silently dropping an escalation.

nodes.name: High priority + existing client?
nodes.notes: The third condition matters: a fallback row means triage failed, so its 'priority' is a placeholder, not a judgement. Escalating on it would page someone because the API had a bad minute.

nodes.name: Fetch original message
nodes.notes: The results row carries the verdict, not the sender. Fetch the message so the Slack post names a person.

parameters.name: =Respond to {{ $('Fetch original message').item.json.from_name || 'client' }} - {{ $('High priority + existing client?').item.json.summary }}

nodes.name: Create advisor task
nodes.notes: A 4-hour due date rather than 'today': the SLA the priority rule implies should be visible in the task system, not just in the prompt.

nodes.name: No escalation
nodes.notes: Everything else is handled by the queue UI. Not every message deserves an interrupt.
